summary: The study describes the fabrication of hollow TiO2 nanoribbon network electrodes for dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using a biotemplating process combining peptide self-assembly and atomic layer deposition (ALD). A thin TiO2 layer was deposited via ALD at 140 ◦C on a peptide template, followed by pyrolysis to create a highly entangled nanotubular TiO2 framework. The process involved calcination at 400 or 500 ◦C to control the crystal phase and crystallite size of the TiO2 nanostructures. The resulting DSSCs exhibited a power conversion efficiency of 3.8%, comparable to conventional TiO2 nanoparticle-based DSSCs.
evidence: A thin TiO2 layer was deposited at the surface of the peptide template via the ALD process. The TTIP was used as a precursor and ammonia (NH3) gas was used as a reactant. The ALD process was performed at 140 ◦C. The peptide template was removed by calcination at 400 or 500 ◦C for 1 h under air. The evolution of the crystal phase and crystallite size of the TiO2 nanostructure was exploited by controlling the calcination temperature.
